objects.paraphrase: Where the space under a stair is enclosed and accessible, its walls, underside and soffits need a gypsum board layer on the space side.

interpretability.rationale: Q3: the gypsum protection applies to 'enclosed' space under stairs; 'enclosed' is not a defined term, and the Review Board had to answer whether open, uncovered stud framing is enclosed (no).

ambiguous_terms.issue: Not defined in IRC Chapter 2 (checked on the UpCodes VRC 2021 text).
Unclear whether a space with an open end but a partial wall counts.

determinations.body: Virginia State Building Code Technical Review Board
determinations.binding_effect: Formal Review Board interpretation, published in the Board's 2021-edition interpretation booklet (September 2026) as still applicable. The Board's interpretations apply statewide to the USBC.
determinations.code_at_issue: VCC (VRC) 2015 edition, carried into the 2021-edition booklet
determinations.holding_summary: Question: if open stud framing is installed under a stairway in an unfinished basement with no drywall or other covering, is the space 'enclosed'? Answer: No. So the under-stair gypsum protection does not apply to open, uncovered framing.

verification.notes: Booklet header: 'Containing Interpretations Applicable to the 2021 Editions', dated September 2026. Its preface still says '2018 edition' in one sentence (an internal inconsistency in the booklet).

candidate_clarification.note: Consider stating that the space is enclosed when wall and soffit coverings conceal the framing on all sides, consistent with Interpretation 1/2021.
